strengths: Tackles an important and pressing challenge in learned 3D point cloud compression: achieving cross-domain generalization and handling diverse densities (from sparse LiDAR to dense meshes and 3D Gaussian splats) with a single universal model.

The Universal Context Model (UCM) provides a well-motivated combination of spatial checkerboard grouping and channel-wise sub-symbol decomposition (splitting 8-bit occupancy into two 4-bit parts), effectively balancing inter-voxel spatial priors with intra-channel sparsity robustness.

The Instance-Adaptive Fine-Tuning (IAFT) strategy is computationally pragmatic: by freezing the backbone and caching intermediate features, only the final lightweight prediction heads are updated and compressed with DeepCABAC, delivering tangible rate savings on out-of-distribution instances without the extreme optimization latency of standard implicit neural representations.

Extensive benchmarking across 15 diverse datasets (covering standard indoor/outdoor benchmarks, modern reconstruction outputs such as VGGT and 3DGS, and corrupted point clouds) convincingly validates the compression ratio gains over both traditional codecs (G-PCC v23) and competitive learning-based baselines.
weaknesses: Encoding latency overhead from IAFT: While decoding latency is very competitive (0.46s), the encoding time increases notably with fine-tuning (from ~0.44s up to 2.84s at default 200 iterations, and over 12s at 800 iterations), which may limit real-time streaming or edge deployment scenarios.

The extension to lossy compression in Section 3.4 is described only briefly (relying on transmitting point count k and selecting top-k occupied voxels); a deeper discussion in the main text on rate-distortion optimization and distortion metrics across scales would strengthen the completeness of the manuscript.

In Table 1, comparing Ours-U (trained on a large composite dataset) against category-specific baselines trained only on KITTI introduces a potential training data scale confound, although the authors mention baseline-U models in the appendix.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental challenge in learned 3D point cloud compression: bridging the generalization gap across diverse densities (from sparse LiDAR to dense object and scene scans) and handling out-of-distribution (OOD) data.

The proposed Universal Context Model (UCM) elegantly combines 3D spatial checkerboard grouping with channel-wise occupancy code factorization, effectively exploiting both local spatial context and intra-code dependencies.

The Instance-Adaptive Fine-Tuning (IAFT) paradigm effectively fuses explicit hierarchical compression with implicit neural parameter adaptation. By updating only the compact final prediction heads, it achieves fast convergence and ensures that the bitrate saved in entropy coding comfortably exceeds the bitstream cost of the transmitted weights.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 15 diverse datasets (including standard LiDAR, dense photogrammetry/Gaussian Splatting coordinates, and synthesized corrupted point clouds), showing superior compression ratio gains (-10.75% over GPCC v23 with a single unified model) compared to existing learning-based codecs.
Fast decoding speed (0.46s) suitable for practical downstream rendering/consumption, with configurable trade-offs during encoding.
weaknesses: The encoding complexity is noticeably increased when IAFT is active (ranging from ~2.8s to >12s), which limits its applicability in real-time streaming or low-latency sensor capture scenarios.

Key theoretical foundations (Theorems 1 and 2 mentioned in Section 3.2) and the detailed operational mechanics of the lossy compression mode (Section 3.4) are heavily relegated to the appendix, leaving parts of the main text somewhat incomplete on self-contained theoretical justification.
Several entries in Table 1 for baseline comparisons (such as Unicorn) are missing due to closed-source availability, which slightly obscures direct comparison on the newer benchmarks.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental and challenging problem in 3D data compression: achieving true generalization across drastically different point cloud modalities (e.g., dense CAD/scans, sparse LiDAR, and 3D Gaussian Splatting) using a single universal model.

The proposed Universal Context Model (UCM) provides an effective formulation combining 3D checkerboard spatial grouping with channel-wise nibble decomposition, successfully bridging the gap between local spatial context and sparsity-robust channel modeling.

The Instance-Adaptive Fine-Tuning (IAFT) strategy cleverly bridges explicit neural entropy modeling and implicit neural representations (INRs); by caching backbone features and fine-tuning only the lightweight prediction heads encoded with DeepCABAC, it achieves rapid instance adaptation with favorable rate-distortion trade-offs.

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across 15 diverse datasets, demonstrating clear compression ratio improvements over established baselines (GPCC v23, SparsePCGC, RENO, OctAttention, and TopNet) under both category-specific and universal single-model settings.

Informative ablation studies that isolate the impact of spatial convolution, spatial grouping, channel grouping, and the bitstream overhead incurred by weight transmission versus geometry bitrate savings.
weaknesses: Encoding latency overhead from instance adaptation: although decoding remains fast (~0.46s), the encoding time increases to 2.84s (at 200 iterations) or over 12s (at 800 iterations), which poses challenges for real-time streaming applications such as autonomous driving LiDAR feeds.

Heuristic deployment of IAFT: as mentioned in Section 4.1, IAFT is selectively applied only to 'M' and 'H' test splits rather than uniformly across all data, raising questions about whether an automated criterion exists for determining when an incoming point cloud is sufficiently out-of-distribution to justify the fine-tuning overhead.

The treatment of lossy compression in Section 3.4 is brief; the rate-distortion mechanism relies primarily on transmitting a target point count k per scale, but the main text lacks in-depth discussion on rate control granularity and distortion optimization relative to standard operational rate-distortion curves.

strengths: Compelling framework addressing a fundamental bottleneck in learned point cloud compression: generalizing across vast variations in density (dense meshes, sparse LiDAR, novel 3DGS coordinates) using a single universal model.

Technically sound integration of coarse-grained spatial partitioning (checkerboard pattern at the occupancy code level) and fine-grained channel partitioning (sub-symbol decomposition), supported by theoretical proofs in Theorems 1 and 2 regarding model equivalence and receptive field expansion.

Clever formulation of Instance-Adaptive Fine-Tuning (IAFT): caching frozen backbone features and optimizing only the lightweight prediction heads enables fast convergence (within seconds) while keeping the transmitted weight payload negligible compared to geometry entropy gains.

Exceptionally extensive empirical evaluation across 15 diverse datasets covering in-distribution, out-of-distribution (VGGT, 3DGS), and procedurally perturbed scans (noise, downsampling, deformation), consistently achieving state-of-the-art lossless and lossy compression performance.
Thorough ablation studies addressing key modules, spatial/channel grouping combinations, quantization step sizes, weight entropy coder choices, and training data mixture ratios.
weaknesses: For lossy compression, the framework transitions from the multi-stage spatial-channel UCM context model to a single-stage model to prevent sequential error propagation, making the lossy extension less tightly coupled with the core UCM architecture.

While IAFT is significantly faster than traditional coordinate-based INRs, the encoding latency (up to 2.84 s for 200 iterations and ~12 s for 800 iterations) remains noticeably higher than purely feed-forward models like RENO (0.22 s), which may limit its application in real-time streaming contexts.

Several comparative baselines (e.g., Unicorn) could not be benchmarked across all 15 datasets due to lack of open-source code, leaving some performance comparisons dependent on previously published numbers on a subset of datasets.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental and challenging problem in learned point cloud compression: building a single, universal model capable of generalizing across widely varying point cloud densities (dense object/human captures, large-scale indoor scenes, sparse LiDAR, and irregular 3D Gaussian Splatting/VGGT data) without model collapse on out-of-distribution (OOD) data.

Principled context modeling: The Universal Context Model (UCM) elegantly synergizes coarse-grained spatial grouping (3D checkerboard) and fine-grained channel grouping directly at the 8-bit occupancy code scale. The theoretical justification (Theorems 1 and 2 in the supplementary material) providing receptive field expansion under sparse convolutions offers strong support for this design.

Effective explicit-implicit hybrid adaptation: The Instance-Adaptive Fine-Tuning (IAFT) strategy achieves rapid per-instance adaptation by freezing the backbone and tuning only the lightweight classification heads using cached features. The bitrate overhead incurred by transmitting the quantized head parameters is thoroughly evaluated and demonstrated to be smaller than the resulting geometry bitrate savings on OOD samples.

Comprehensive empirical benchmark: The evaluation across 15 datasets (including standard MPEG/AVS test sets, modern reconstruction outputs, and procedurally corrupted benchmarks) provides convincing evidence of generalization and consistently outperforms GPCC v23 and recent learning-based methods in both lossless and lossy scenarios.
weaknesses: Manual trigger for IAFT: In the experiments (Table 1), IAFT is applied only to Medium and Hard datasets, while Easy datasets bypass it. In a fully autonomous practical deployment, the system needs an automatic decision rule (e.g., evaluating whether the predicted rate reduction justifies the parameter bitstream overhead). The manuscript would benefit from specifying or formalizing this automated selection mechanism.

Bifurcated lossy compression strategy: The lossless framework is unified, but the lossy extension bifurcates into two distinct mechanisms: scale truncation for sparse LiDAR versus transmitting total count k with top-k decoding for dense clouds. This somewhat weakens the claim of a completely seamless, unified compression pipeline across all data types.

Encoding latency in latency-critical scenarios: While decoding is fast (~0.46s), the encoding time with IAFT (defaulting to 2.84s and extending up to ~12s depending on channel count and iterations) remains high for real-time LiDAR streaming applications. A clearer delineation between real-time operational settings (e.g., zero/low-iteration IAFT) and high-efficiency offline archiving would clarify the target use cases.

Minor presentation issues: Figures 1 and 2 rely on informal emojis (smileys), which detracts slightly from formal academic presentation. In Table 9, several entries are left blank ('/') due to baseline incompatibility, which could be explained more clearly directly in the table header or text.

strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation benchmark spanning 15 distinct datasets, encompassing dense human scans, sparse LiDAR, neural 3D representations (3D Gaussian Splatting), feed-forward reconstructions (VGGT), and procedurally corrupted stress tests (RS, NS, CS).

Effective Universal Context Model (UCM) design that successfully unifies spatial checkerboard grouping with channel-wise sub-symbol decomposition at the occupancy code scale, supported by theoretical analysis of receptive field expansion and information equivalence.

The Instance-Adaptive Fine-Tuning (IAFT) paradigm smartly bridges explicit entropy coding and implicit parameter adaptation. Freezing the feature backbone, caching representations, and fine-tuning only the lightweight prediction heads achieves fast convergence (seconds) while correctly accounting for the weight transmission overhead in the overall bitrate.

Strong empirical performance: the unified model variant ('Ours-U') achieves superior generalization on out-of-distribution point clouds compared to category-specific baselines and traditional codecs like G-PCC v23, advancing towards practical universal point cloud compression.
Thorough ablation studies analyzing spatial vs. channel groupings, tuning iterations, weight quantization, and data mixture ratios.
weaknesses: Asymmetric comparison in Table 1: 'Ours' and 'Ours-U' employ test-time adaptation (IAFT with 200 iterations) on medium and hard datasets, whereas all competing learning-based baselines (e.g., SparsePCGC, RENO, OctAttention, TopNet) are evaluated strictly in feedforward mode without instance-level fine-tuning. Evaluating whether baselines benefit equally from head fine-tuning would provide a fairer comparison.

Latency constraints for real-time deployment: While an encoding latency of ~1.35s to 2.84s is significantly faster than training coordinate-based MLPs from scratch, it remains prohibitive for real-time streaming applications (e.g., LiDAR processing at 10–20 Hz). The computational overhead of test-time optimization restricts its utility primarily to offline storage or asynchronous transmission.

Lossy compression extension is relatively ad-hoc compared to the primary lossless formulation, relying on transmitting the ground-truth point count and selecting top-k probabilities, which exhibits diminishing returns and less competitive behavior on certain complex geometries.
Minor presentation issues, such as typographical errors ('IImplementation' in Table 4) and occasional missing comparative baseline curves in lossy evaluations.
